It's been brewing a few years now, but there seems to have been a sudden jump from "Fat people are seen occasionally" to "Fat people are becoming more and more of the norm."

I took my vacation to Seoul this year. I was happily expecting to be surrounded by the most beautiful people on the planet. For the most part it was true, but there were way more hams than I expected. Granted, nothing like we see here in America, but damn... I saw at least 3 or 4 every day. :(

The thing about the Korean (well, Asian in general) is that the BMI numbers are lower than for non-Asians. This is due to a genetic predisposition to pack fat on the midsection, putting them at risk for obesity-related issues at a lower BMI. This means "ham" starts lower in Korea.
With all that high carb/fat street food in Korea, I'm surprised it took that long to get to that weight.

The issue was both frequency and activity. Anyone who's been to a Korean gym will tell you two things: they're widely empty and those that do go usually just end up slowly walking on a treadmill (slowly, so they can watch their favourite TV drama on the screen). In other words, even those that work out don't really "work out" (with few exceptions, of course...there are Korean bodybuilders and runners and such). Most people don't even do that, and many work sedentary jobs and finish work by going home or to an internet cafe and being sedentary. This is based on job, of course; I don't think I've seen fat cops but I have unfortunately seen fatty fat soldiers.

Food is a lot easier to come by lately, and the culture highly encourages lots and lots of eating. While Koreans will tell you you're fat, they're also incredibly shocked when you eat less at a meal. Imagine that: they tell you to your face that you're fat and need to stop eating so much, and then they have no idea why you eat less at meals. This isn't everyone, of course, but holy shit it happens often.
